newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares correcting after new records.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares correcting after new records.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased back from fresh record highs on Monday afternoon as trading thinned in a downward correction that dealers said would probably last at least through midday on Tuesday.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index at 1300 GMT set a record 507.75, up from Friday's 495.57 close, but traders said a sell-off had then begun. Utility Mosenergo, the most traded share of the day, fell to $1.606 at 1332, off a daily high of about $1.700 and down from Friday's $1.640 close.

"In this type of volatile environment a few percentage points wouldn't be a problem," ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko said of potential losses. He said the market would be volatile for a few days.
"The dust has to settle," said a Moscow trader who added that Western investors had withdrawn bids worth between $200,000 and $500,000, which are crucial to market liquidity.

Oil producer LUKoil which gained about 50 percent last week eased to $22.40 at 1355 from $23.20 on Friday. Norilsk Nickel rose to $11.35 from $10.95 after Uneximbank said it would sell a 38 percent government stake it manages.

The downward correction was seen in the dozen leading liquid shares such as Mosenergo, which had gained almost 30 percent last week on an influx of new funds that fuelled index and market turnover records but left traders nervous.

Russian operators as well as a few Westerners were seen taking profit after the run-up. "We traded up to new index highs, but there was not much follow-through from New York," Kizenko said of Monday trade. Brokers said foreign buyers were still eager for shares but were waiting to see where prices would settle before they resumed buying.
